problems.problem: Potential loss or slow follow-up of after-hours and weekend residential and commercial leads outside the stated Monday–Friday 8:00 AM–4:30 PM window.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The site states availability from Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and uses a standard web contact form and phone number with no visible instant-response or online scheduling mechanism.

problems.problem: Manual lead transfer from website contact form submissions and phone inquiries into back-office scheduling or field-service software.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The contact page relies on a standard website form component without visible direct integration into a field-service management (FSM) widget, though internal email or webhook automations cannot be ruled out from public pages.

problems.problem: Difficulty tracking marketing return on ad spend, close rates, and revenue across two separate operating markets (Boise, ID and Lexington, KY).
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The website loads a tracking tag (AW-805112476) and promotes multiple discount offers across two state operations, which could create fragmented reporting if ad spend, job booking, and accounting systems are not unified.

existingSolutions.solution: Built-in form notifications and native integrations within the existing website platform (crofts-electric-boise.squarespace.com)
existingSolutions.addresses: Basic email notification and confirmation emails when a visitor submits the website contact form.

existingSolutions.solution: Off-the-shelf Field Service Management (FSM) software with native web booking, call tracking, and automated SMS lead response (e.g., ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, or Jobber)
existingSolutions.addresses: Lead intake, instant customer reply, dispatching, estimating, and basic revenue reporting.

forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: One-week audit ($500 fixed price, credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days) to measure how many phone calls, web form leads, and written estimates slip through, especially outside the 8:00 AM–4:30 PM weekday window.
forgexSolutions.problem: Unconfirmed volume of missed calls, slow web-form follow-ups, or unclosed written estimates.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Before buying new software or custom automation, a baseline audit establishes whether a genuine lead-leakage problem exists and quantifies its impact.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Automated pipeline ($1,800 setup plus $149/month) that captures every web form submission and missed call, sends an instant reply within two minutes, and pushes structured lead records (including discount eligibility and project type) into field-service software with follow-up reminders.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential delay in responding to after-hours/weekend inquiries and manual entry of website form leads into field-service tools.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Website contact forms do not natively push normalized lead records, discount tags, and two-minute SMS/email follow-up sequences into third-party contractor scheduling tools without custom integration.

forgexSolutions.name: Owner's Monday numbers
forgexSolutions.description: Weekly one-page summary ($1,200 setup plus $99/month) combining booked revenue, close rate, average ticket, cost per booked job by lead source, and accounts receivable across operations.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential lack of consolidated visibility into ad performance, discount impact, and job profitability across the Boise, ID and Lexington, KY locations.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Standard accounting or field-service dashboards rarely combine ad account spend, multi-location close rates, and receivables into a single automated weekly owner digest without cross-system integration.

feasibility.explanation: Capturing leads from the website form and routing them with instant replies is technically straightforward, but full end-to-end integration depends on which field-service management (FSM), phone system, and accounting software Crofts Electric uses internally—none of which are observable from the public website.

aiDelivery.explanation: Deterministic workflow automation should handle form ingestion, lead creation, CRM/FSM synchronization, and weekly metric aggregation. AI agents can assist with classifying free-text project inquiries (e.g., panel upgrade vs. commercial fit-out vs. property management request) and drafting initial responses, but cannot replace deterministic data pipelines or licensed electrician estimating.

humanReview: All written cost estimates and technical electrical assessments must be reviewed and approved by a licensed journeyman or master electrician.
Verification of customer discount eligibility (new customer, repeat customer, senior, first responder, or active military) prior to final invoicing.
Human handoff for complex commercial, construction bidding, property management, or emergency electrical troubleshooting inquiries.

risks.description: Automated SMS or voice follow-ups triggered by web forms or missed calls must comply with TCPA opt-in and consent requirements.

An AI or automated responder must never provide electrical safety advice, troubleshooting instructions, or binding price quotes, as improper electrical guidance creates severe safety and liability hazards.

Customer contact details, property addresses, and commercial client information must be transmitted securely with least-privilege API access between the website, messaging tools, and back-office software.

commercial.implementationCost: Revenue Leak Check: $500 fixed price (credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days); Lead-to-job pipeline: $1,800 setup plus $149/month; Owner's Monday numbers: $1,200 setup plus $99/month.
assumptions: The website does not publish dollar prices for service calls, hourly labor, or installations (only percentage discounts of 10% and 15%), so illustrative commercial value cannot be calculated from site prices.

discovery.outreachSubject: Question about lead follow-up at Crofts Electric Boise
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [redacted],

I was reviewing Crofts Electric's Boise website and noticed that your office hours run Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with project inquiries coming in by phone or through your website contact form.

At ForgeX, we work with owner-led electrical and home-service contractors to audit and automate lead intake and owner reporting for a fixed price. Because I can't see your internal systems from the outside, I don't know if after-hours lead response or manual form entry is a bottleneck for your team right now—or if you already have software handling it.

If you're curious how many calls, web inquiries, or written estimates might be slipping through between Boise and Lexington, we offer a one-week Revenue Leak Check for a $500 fixed price (which is credited in full if you order any fix within 30 days), as well as a fixed-price Lead-to-job pipeline ($1,800 setup + $149/month). We don't promise specific revenue outcomes, and if your current setup already covers this, we'll tell you straight up.

Would you be open to a brief 10-minute conversation next week to see if this is relevant to your operations?

Best regards,

[FOUNDER_NAME]
[FOUNDER_TITLE], ForgeX
[FOUNDER_PHONE]
[FOUNDER_EMAIL]
[FORGEX_POSTAL_ADDRESS]

If you prefer not to receive future emails from me, please reply with "unsubscribe" or use [OPT_OUT_LINK_OR_INSTRUCTIONS] and I will remove you immediately.

sourcesUsed.usedFor: Business identity, Boise service areas, operating hours (Mon–Fri 8am–4:30pm), phone number ([redacted]), Idaho and Kentucky license numbers, services offered, promotional discounts, and homepage scripts/hosts.
Founder identity ([redacted]), parent entity (RC Electric LLC), expansion from Lexington, KY to Boise, ID, and gtag.js script presence.
Staffing policy (only journeyman and master electricians) and qualification standards.
Contact workflow (web form and phone call), form component script, and gtag.js tracking script.
Discount structure and customer self-reporting instructions for promotional discounts.
Property management electrical services and consultation call-to-action.

limitations: Total employee headcount (and whether the company falls within ForgeX's 10-to-75 staff target range) is not stated on the website.
No dollar prices for services or labor are published on the website, preventing a supportable commercial value calculation.
Back-office software (such as field-service management, CRM, accounting, or call-answering services) cannot be observed from the public website.
One internal link on the About page (https://www.croftselectricboise.com/trusted-experts-boise-electricians-lexington-electricians) returned HTTP 404 (not found).
Whether the AW-805112476 tag is actively receiving paid ad traffic today cannot be confirmed from the static page source alone.

qualification.rationale: Crofts Electric is an owner-led electrical contractor (founded by [redacted]) operating in Boise, ID and Lexington, KY, with an observable advertising/conversion tag (AW-805112476), weekday-only stated hours (Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM), a basic website contact form, and a business phone channel ([redacted]). However, staff headcount (10–75 employees) cannot be verified from the website, and all operational problems (such as missed after-hours leads or manual lead entry) remain unconfirmed hypotheses rather than confirmed customer problems. Under ForgeX's qualification rules, a plausible fit whose problems are hypotheses only qualifies as 'pursue later'.
